findings.title: Copy-paste error in Objects.requireNonNull null check
findings.body: The fourth Objects.requireNonNull call passes `grantType` (not `rawTokenId`) but uses the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. As a result: (1) a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted and will later cause an NPE inside the encoder, and (2) a null `grantType` is reported with a misleading error message. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: Matcher isAccessTokenId has inverted logic
findings.body: In `isAccessTokenId`, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (i.e. test FAILS) when the grant shortcut matches the expected one, and proceeds (i.e. test PASSES based only on the UUID check) when it does NOT match. The condition is backwards: it should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Used in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken, so any test asserting on the access-token id will give the opposite of the expected result.

findings.title: Matcher isAccessTokenId slices wrong characters for the grant shortcut
findings.body: The encoded prefix has layout [session 0-1][token 2-3][grant 4-5], so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5. The matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which returns the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant type, not the grant type itself. It should be `substring(4, 6)`. Combined with the inverted logic, the matcher never actually verifies the grant type and accepts any 6-char prefix as long as the UUID part is valid.

findings.title: TokenContextEncoderSpi marked internal, contradicts stated extensibility goal
findings.body: `isInternal()` returns `true`, which in Keycloak restricts the SPI to a single implementation (the default). The PR description explicitly motivates the SPI by saying 'provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider'. To match that intent, `isInternal()` must return `false`, otherwise third parties cannot supply an alternative encoder.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed without notice
findings.body: The previous public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted by this PR. The constructor was on a public nested class of a public SPI, so any downstream code that created derived or copied Contexts will fail to compile. The PR description does not call out this removal, and there is no replacement, so this is an undocumented SPI breaking change.

findings.title: Constant name GRANT_TYPE is misleading
findings.body: `public static final String GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE;` resolves to the literal string `"grant_type"`, which is a key name used as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key, not a grant-type value. The name suggests a grant type such as `authorization_code`. Either the constant should be renamed to make clear it is a session-context attribute key (e.g. `CLIENT_SESSION_CTX_GRANT_TYPE`) or the Javadoc should explain it is the OAuth2 parameter/attribute name, not a grant type value, to avoid misuse such as `ctx.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.AUTHORIZATION_CODE)` style calls.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null encodedTokenId
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId(String encodedTokenId)` immediately calls `encodedTokenId.indexOf(':')` with no null check. If a caller passes null (for example from `token.getId()` returning null), this throws an NPE instead of returning the UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/encodedTokenId context the method otherwise provides for unencoded ids. It should guard against null and treat it the same as an old (unprefixed) id.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext NPEs on null userSession
findings.body: `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` is dereferenced for both `getPersistenceState()` and `isOffline()` without a null check. In some flows (e.g. when a client session is not yet bound to a user session, or in OID4VCI issuance paths that build a token without a persisted user session) this can be null, producing an NPE in the encoder. The provider should treat a null userSession as UNKNOWN rather than failing token issuance.

findings.title: Dynamic grant-type insertion is racy and can corrupt the shortcut maps
findings.body: Both `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do a non-atomic check-then-put into the `ConcurrentHashMap`s. Two threads can simultaneously take the `null` branch and both write. More importantly, nothing prevents a new grant factory from registering with a shortcut that collides with an existing one after `postInit`, which silently overwrites the existing entry in `grantsByShortcuts` and corrupts lookups in both directions; the startup-only size check in `postInit` does not protect against this hot path.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but implementation uses 2 letters
findings.body: The new `getShortcut()` Javadoc reads 'usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants', but every built-in factory introduced by this PR (AuthorizationCode, ClientCredentials, Permission, PreAuthorizedCode, RefreshToken, ResourceOwnerPassword, TokenExchange, Ciba, Device) defines a 2-character shortcut. Either the Javadoc should be corrected to say '2-character shortcut' or the contract should permit variable length; otherwise implementers are likely to follow the comment and supply the wrong length.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException instead of the specific type
findings.body: The test catches bare `RuntimeException` and ignores the variable, so it would pass on any unexpected throw (e.g. NPE, IllegalStateException, ClassCastException) and would not catch a regression where the method silently returns instead of throwing. It should catch `IllegalArgumentException` (the type the implementation actually throws) and ideally assert the message, so the test specifically validates the documented behavior.
